issue_plan.name: Native acceptance and repository context
issue_plan.summary: These ten issues implement #564's first ten remaining steps in order, one plumbing change per pull request. They finish configured Go acceptance, add exact pytest, Vitest and Jest evidence, and apply repository conventions, trust rules and context. Configuration drafting with invariant init, the generated CI gate and external intake with end-to-end factory coverage remain after this plan; external intake stays disabled.

issues.title: Validate Go runtime lifecycles and return local acceptance evidence
issues.body:
Finish the local collector over internal/plumbing/go_producer.go and process_transport_local.go: validate #538's Go lifecycle events and convert them to RepositoryAcceptanceEvidence behind local RunAcceptance. Shared orchestration, Docker transport and compiler attribution follow in the next three issues.

- The fixture supplies process, file and channel mechanics, never outcomes. Unsupported commands stop at Select, before preparation; failed discovery prevents collection.
- Pin the fresh InvocationID, full (part, framework, file, selector) identity, discovered package, source digest and captured-execution digest.
- Require one selection, authentic start and terminal per exact test, with parent/child lifecycle for nested and parallel tests (interleaving isn't reordering); no ancestor, prefix, sibling or parameter case stands in. Duplicate, stale, contradictory, truncated or mismatched records never qualify.
- Completed pass, assertion failure, panic and selected skip become test passed/failed/skipped; skip qualifies nothing. Zero tests, absent selectors, TestMain exit before m.Run, abrupt exit, interruption or no terminal never complete, with reasons; helper, discovery and compiler failures are setup or refusal.
- #515's trusted fakes and Run/ReadFile/Close-only environments keep their contracts. Partial evidence survives; infrastructure errors veto.
- Keep every captured test_one flag; run verbatim sources offline with only the pinned toolchain and standard library. Inherit the remaining allowance; bounded cleanup leaves no processes.

Acceptance: default tests run real standard-library modules (isolated caches, no Docker or network). Identical bytes fail a real assertion on base and pass after a production-only change; each outcome above happens for real; neighbors and same names elsewhere never match; forged diagnostics on both streams and corrupted real streams, beside real controls, never qualify; cancellation is bounded.

Add separate runtime fixtures; preserve existing acceptance_*, go_* and native_* tests and fakes unchanged. Default adapters, planning admission and external plumbing stay off; legacy Go is unchanged. Update SPEC.md, docs/factory.md and README. Rests on D-0107, D-0108, D-0110, D-0111, D-0121, D-0173, D-0281, D-0282, D-0301, D-0305, D-0311, D-0314, D-0316, D-0321 and D-0327, #538's decision.

Kind: plumbing

issues.title: Integrate real Go acceptance evidence with base, candidate and queue checks
issues.body:
Integrate the preceding local collector through Sandbox.checkRepositoryBase and configured Sandbox.Run in internal/plumbing/repository_acceptance.go, repository_checks.go and checkqueue.go. Complete the shared lifecycle with real Go; the next issue adds Docker with this same collector.

- Extend the existing orchestration with no new runner, scheduler, selector policy or parser. Existing adapter and fake contracts stay valid; only the Go path demands authentic start and terminal.
- Base checks try every independent selector after build, suite or test failures while allowance remains, and need an attributable completed failure for each; none broadcasts to a passing neighbor. Candidates need every applicable command and selector to pass. Go compiler errors are setup/refusal; skipped, refused, running and unstarted results never qualify; setup, transport, cancellation, allowance or cleanup failures veto without erasing completed evidence.
- All work shares the inherited twelve-minute run, capped by caller, sandbox and preparer, and one ten-minute phase started by the first suite test or discovery; nothing resets either, test_one -timeout=0 included. Captured authority beats candidate changes. Each part's environment is removed before its staging and the next part; cleanup gets fifteen uncanceled seconds; the queue slot lasts through it.

Acceptance (default tests, local real-Go fixture, no Docker or network), on both paths: a base assertion failure becomes a candidate pass after a production-only change with identical bytes. Cover pass, assertion failure, panic, skip, zero tests, absent selectors, TestMain exit before m.Run, abrupt exit and missing terminals; mixed results in one package, earlier failing suites, same names across packages, modules, parts, another package's build failure, seam corruption and transport errors beside real controls, forged diagnostics, clipped JSON and queue round-trips, both phase starts, cancellation at each stage, queue contention and cleanup failure.

Add separate integration fixtures; preserve existing acceptance_*, go_* and native_* tests and fakes unchanged, including evidence515's terminal without a running record. Default adapters, planning admission and external plumbing stay off; legacy Go is unchanged. Update SPEC.md, docs/factory.md and README, not yet claiming Docker evidence. Rests on D-0107, D-0108, D-0110, D-0111, D-0121, D-0173, D-0281, D-0282, D-0301, D-0305, D-0311, D-0314, D-0316 and D-0321.

issues.title: Run Go acceptance in prepared Docker environments
issues.body:
Make DockerDependencyRunner.OpenChecks' prepared Go environment supply RunAcceptance, so real base failures and candidate passes work through Sandbox.checkRepositoryBase and configured Sandbox.Run. It completes runtime execution; compiler failures stay setup/refusal until the next issue adds attribution.

- Reuse the identical producer, collector, Select, Discover and lifecycle, with no Docker-specific interpretation; identity, digests, package and InvocationID cross the transport unchanged.
- Carry events on a trusted transport apart from all workload output. Helpers are host-staged outside the candidate tree, using only the pinned image's tools: no Python, host cache, installs or network. Candidate configuration never supplies helpers, commands or transport authority; exits and forged text are never evidence.
- Keep docs/factory.md's prepared-container contract plus GOPROXY=off, GOSUMDB=off, GOTOOLCHAIN=local, GOENV=off, GOWORK=off, captured readonly/vendor policy and disposable caches. Selectors stay arguments, never wrapper source. One environment per part, closed before the next opens; Run, ReadFile, Close and non-Go environments are unchanged.
- All work shares the twelve-minute run and ten-minute phase, shortened by caller and preparer; bounded uncanceled cleanup joins processes and removes container and staging before the queue slot frees. Failures veto, keeping earlier work.

Acceptance: daemon-free default tests replace only the Docker process/transport boundary and check actual Docker argv for image, directory, isolation, offline environment, no pull/build/install or host mounts, one active part and cleanup order, plus transport, cancellation and cleanup failures. Use a separate runtime fixture; preserve existing tests and fakes unchanged, including go_container_accept_test.go and repository_container_accept_test.go. Earlier real-Go default tests stay mandatory, via the same transport abstraction. A documented opt-in test runs the real environment offline in a prepared pinned image (base failure, fix, exact child, skip, abrupt exit, forged output), reporting missing prerequisites without downloading.

Default adapters, planning admission and external plumbing stay off; legacy Go is unchanged. Update SPEC.md, docs/factory.md and README. Rests on D-0107, D-0108, D-0110, D-0111, D-0121, D-0173, D-0281, D-0282, D-0301, D-0305, D-0311, D-0314, D-0316 and D-0321.

Kind: plumbing

issues.title: Attribute proposed-API compiler failures and verify complete Go acceptance
issues.body:
Add proposed-API compiler attribution to Go discovery and acceptance in internal/plumbing and verify the complete adapter through the lower-level configured lifecycle. The next issue enables planning, builder-tool and final-check admission.

- A completed compiler failure counts as base evidence only when the trusted boundary attributes it to the selected acceptance's use of the proposed API: record compile/failed for that invocation and full identity, with source and execution digests and its attribution, not as runtime completion. Diagnostics, a nonzero exit or a failing package or suite prove nothing; ambiguity never counts.
- Never broadcast a compile failure to other selectors in its file, package, module or part, even compiled together. Use normal production files and dependencies under captured policy, never source-only runs or rewritten acceptance. Every base selector fails independently; candidates need completed passes in a fresh run, never compile success, suite passes, cached verdicts, skips or unstarted ones.
- Missing tools, unresolved dependencies, broken discovery, excluded or wrong-file declarations, unrelated invalid source or production failures, interrupted compilation and failed transport are setup, refusal or incomplete, with reasons, distinct from compile and test failures; earlier results survive.

Acceptance (default tests, real standard-library modules, production code): a new-API acceptance fails on base with attributable compile evidence and passes after a production-only change with identical bytes; a passing neighbor in its file or package, or a same name elsewhere, inherits nothing; each failure above yields no evidence, and interruption hits real in-progress compilation. Via checkRepositoryBase and configured Sandbox.Run, each base selector has its own test/failed or compile/failed, and captured authority survives contract, source and binding changes and stale results. Real work consumes later selectors' allowance; earlier runtime and corruption cases still run.

Add new attribution fixtures; preserve existing acceptance_*, go_* and native_* tests and fakes unchanged. Unsupported-framework and no-adapter refusals precede preparation; external plumbing stays off; legacy plans and the unconfigured Go path are unchanged. Update SPEC.md, docs/factory.md and README. Rests on D-0107, D-0108, D-0110, D-0111, D-0121, D-0173, D-0281, D-0282, D-0301, D-0305, D-0311, D-0314, D-0316 and D-0321.

Kind: plumbing

issues.title: Use configured Go evidence in planning and builder checks
issues.body:
Enable the Go adapter and shared lifecycle in internal/plumbing/check.go, build.go, checkqueue.go and internal/formalize/plan.go, leaving no configured Go planning or building follow-up.

- Lift the configured/native refusal only for supported Go acceptance, on the independent base path. A draft is proposable only when every identity has exactly one matching completed eligible failure, so one passing selector invalidates it. Skipped, absent, unfinished or mismatched results never qualify; ordinary command failures supply no evidence; install, startup, cleanup, deadline or cancellation failures veto.
- Candidate Sandbox.Run needs every applicable command and selector to pass through the same lifecycle; a suite pass, the Accepted map or compile success never yields Passed, and failed final checks block approval and readiness. Review and repairs are unchanged.
- Direct execution checks the bytes it runs against the trusted snapshot, refusing changed digests, identities or sources. Staging admits only authorized production changes and Go regressions; a candidate repository.json is never authority.
- The builder tool, fresh final checks and planning's queued check and final validation apply identical registered rules; IPC carries only work identity and location; queues hold the slot through bounded cleanup; runs share one deadline.
- Truncation never hides which selectors passed or didn't complete. pytest, Vitest and Jest are refused before preparation; mixed plans never partially qualify; configured legacy records are refused, not migrated; legacy Go is unchanged.

Acceptance (default real-Go tests, no Docker or network): a draft failing on a committed base passes after a production-only change, a pass-plus-fail pair blocks, a proposed-API compile failure qualifies only its selection, and each refusal and veto above is tested. In an IPC builder fixture, tool and fresh final check run the same bytes, reject forged output and replaced authority, and the final check sees edits after a tool pass, in standalone and shared queues; planner tool and proposal agree. A documented opt-in pinned-image test runs base failure to candidate pass offline, cleaning up after every outcome; enabled, missing Docker fails.

Update SPEC.md, README and docs/factory.md: configured Go acceptance works; pytest/Vitest/Jest and external intake don't. Rests on D-0107, D-0108, D-0110, D-0111, D-0121, D-0173, D-0281, D-0282, D-0301, D-0305, D-0311, D-0314, D-0316 and D-0321.

issues.title: Collect exact pytest acceptance results in the offline runner
issues.body:
Add a pytest adapter with the same captured configuration, independent invocation, identity and offline environment as Go; Python acceptance files are new regular discoverable test files. TypeScript follows in the next issue.

- Run test_one once per exact node ID relative to the part (function, method or explicitly selected parameter case), matched literally without shell evaluation or -k. Exactly one collected test must match; a class, file, ambiguous selector or parameter group is refused. Unsafe templates are refused before launch; pytest is never fetched.
- A factory-controlled pytest integration, never console text, binds collection, execution and terminal status to the invocation and node ID. A candidate pass needs the selected call and the run, teardown included, to complete. Skips, xfail/xpass, deselection, no tests, duplicate IDs, absent calls, incomplete runs and conflicting evidence are neither pass nor base failure; missing pytest, plugin or import configuration, fixture setup or teardown and environment failures are setup.
- A completed collection or import failure qualifies only when evidence ties it to the selected source's use of a missing proposed API, with a working framework; unrelated imports, missing distributions, broken conftest, malformed setup or ambiguity refuse the draft; exit status or text never suffices. Completed assertion failures qualify on base; each selector later needs a normal candidate pass.
- Keep shared deadlines, cancellation, queue, cleanup and source protection; timeout or interruption voids base evidence even after a failure. Draft, builder-tool and final checks use this adapter, with no suite or legacy fallback.

Acceptance: real pytest in a pinned offline fixture, not a fake, fails on base and passes after a change with unchanged sources and selectors, across same-named files, two parts, class methods and a punctuated parameter case; a passing selector beside a failing one, each refusal above, forged text, replay and tampering never qualify. Default Go tests need no Docker or network; an enabled opt-in pinned-image suite fails, not skips, without prerequisites.

Update SPEC.md, README and docs/factory.md for pytest; external plumbing stays off. Rests on D-0107, D-0108, D-0121, D-0173, D-0281, D-0282, D-0301, D-0305 and the earlier native steps.

issues.title: Collect exact Vitest and Jest acceptance results and complete native coverage
issues.body:
Add separate Vitest and Jest adapters for TypeScript parts under the same identity, test_one, environment and completion rules, plus cross-framework fixtures completing native acceptance; external intake remains deferred.

- Accept new regular test or spec files, TSX where supported. Select one exact file and full nested title via test_one, literally, so a same-named test elsewhere can't match; titles stay inert arguments. Run once, never watching; refuse unsafe templates. test.each/it.each cases qualify only when the title selects one concrete case; duplicates or multi-case patterns are ambiguous.
- Factory-controlled reporters supply evidence by each framework's lifecycle, bound to invocation, framework, part, file and title. Console output and forged reports stay diagnostics; missing, stale, conflicting or mismatched artifacts, even on exit zero, and candidate reporters or prewritten artifacts are never evidence. No tests, skip/todo, expected failures, never-run tests, worker death and incomplete shutdown never pass.
- Reject a proposal if any selector passes, is absent or skipped, or lacks completed attributable failure; assertion failures stay distinct from hook, setup, transform, configuration, runner, npm and tool errors; a transform, import or type failure qualifies only when attributable to the selected test's use of proposed code.
- Share budgets without renewal, offline, one environment at a time; frameworks come from locked dependencies, with no installs or Python in Node images.

Acceptance: real Vitest and Jest fixtures fail on base and pass after a production change with unchanged tests, covering nested and punctuated titles, a parameterized case, cross-file and cross-part names, passing beside failing, a proposed-API case per framework and each refusal above; enabled opt-in pinned-image fixtures fail without prerequisites; default Go tests run offline. A mixed Go, pytest, Vitest and Jest repository with colliding names checks each selector separately, rejects tampering through builder tool and final check, keeps legacy Go locks passing, and covers aggregate Check/Passed.

Update SPEC.md, README and docs/factory.md for all four frameworks; external intake stays off. Rests on D-0107, D-0108, D-0121, D-0173, D-0281, D-0282, D-0301, D-0305 and the earlier native steps.

issues.title: Apply repository test conventions to staging and scope
issues.body:
Extend the existing regression-test allowance to configured repositories, using the repository context and native tests from the preceding issues. A build may write its plan's named files and add new regular regression tests in the touched code's test scope, following that part's framework conventions. This must support Python test directories and TypeScript colocated or separate tests without treating arbitrary files in a part as writable tests.

Use one policy across internal/plumbing/stage.go, writable-file discovery, formatting, sandbox selection, final copying and internal/scope/scope.go. Determine additions against the original checkout throughout builder repairs, and against the diff's merge base in CI. A later repair may change or remove a regression test that this build added. Existing unnamed tests, other production files, unrelated parts, test configuration, ratified acceptance sources and plan records remain protected. Keep regular-file checks, including refusal of symbolic and hard links. Preserve Invariant's precise Go package and embedded-asset ownership behavior.

Acceptance: new conventional regression files are admitted and executed for Go, Python and TypeScript; a separate test directory can belong to touched source; unrelated tests and production files disguised as tests are refused. Exercise staging, copy-back and CI scope with the same cases. Cover repair removal, a base branch that deleted an existing test after divergence, a deleted package, changes outside the plan and attempts to change the pinned acceptance tests. The configured allowance must not depend on candidate edits to repository policy.

Keep SPEC.md, the README (at most 400 lines), and docs/factory.md accurate for this step. Whoever merges it records its decision before the next step.

issues.title: Hold each repository's trusted changes for a person
issues.body:
Use the base-branch repository contract to compute the trusted base for configured external repositories. Always include CI configuration and the gate workflow, .invariant/repository.json, repository agent rules such as root and nested AGENTS.md, and the file's additional trusted paths. Protect configuration that supplies agents' instructions or tools as well. Invariant continues to use its current plumbing.TrustedBase and current CI-path restrictions.

For configured external plumbing, allow explicitly planned CI files through plan validation and scope, while classifying them as human-merge changes. This replaces the unconditional .github rejection only for that profile. Document that publishing workflow changes requires credentials permitted to do so; ordinary plumbing does not require that permission. A missing permission must produce an actionable human handoff, never a ready or merged success. Keep Invariant's App permission policy unchanged.

Carry trusted classification through proposals, scope results, publication, retries and the last pre-merge check. Reuse the existing protocol's human-merge hold rather than changing its proved transitions. Recompute from actual changed paths and authoritative base rules, not the plan's displayed Trusted list. Candidate deletion or weakening of a trust declaration cannot authorize its own merge; revalidate against the current base before merging and stop on an incompatible configuration change.

Acceptance: repository-file, CI, root/nested agent-rule and custom-trusted edits wait for a person and their drafts are not automatically readied, including after retry. An ordinary in-scope change remains eligible for automatic merge. Cover removal of a trust entry, forged Trusted metadata and base movement. Invariant's existing trusted-path and CI-refusal tests retain their results. Update docs/factory-app.md for the external workflow-edit prerequisite.

Keep SPEC.md, the README (at most 400 lines), and docs/factory.md accurate for this step. Whoever merges it records its decision before the next step.

Keep external issue intake disabled; exercise this configured profile below that gate.

issues.title: Give planning, build and review agents repository context
issues.body:
Make plumbing agents and factory posts describe the repository they are working on. Use the trusted context from the base configuration for planning, initial builds, fallbacks, repairs and read-only reviews: applicable agent rules, which documents describe the current repository, part ownership, commands, native acceptance selectors, regression conventions and human-merge paths. Ensure repository rules actually reach each role's workspace and prompt without replacing the factory's immutable plan and scope boundaries.

Update internal/formalize/plan.go, internal/plumbing/prompt.go and their callers. Also adapt internal/factory/plancomments.go: proposals must show native test sources and selectors honestly, and pull requests must describe the configured checks rather than always promising gofmt/go vet. Include repository context in plans of issues where needed, while leaving modeled-project synthesis behavior alone.

Invariant's SPEC.md, README's 400-line budget, decision journal and merger-work rules apply to Invariant as today. Another repository follows its own declared rules and current-state documents; a file merely named SPEC.md or README.md does not import Invariant's policies. Do not add decision-followup automation: #452 leaves each step's decision to its merger.

Acceptance: inspect planner, builder, repair and reviewer requests for Go/Python/TypeScript repositories, including one without SPEC.md or decisions/ and a monorepo with nested rules. Their prompts and posts name the correct framework, checks and documents, and do not impose absent Invariant documents or Go-only test rules. Preserve the existing Invariant documentation/prompt tests and review/repair budgets.

Keep SPEC.md, the README (at most 400 lines), and docs/factory.md accurate for this step. Whoever merges it records its decision before the next step.

External issue intake stays disabled pending configuration drafting and generated CI.
